concerns.text: Task T014 authorizes a 'Miedema model approximation' fallback for missing pairwise enthalpy data. This violates Constitution Principle VI (Thermodynamic Feature Engineering Integrity) which mandates descriptors be derived 'strictly from the elemental properties defined in the standard Periodic Table' and forbids 'unverified proxy values'. The task effectively relaxes the FR-002 requirement to use standard formulas.

Task T029b instructs the system to 'switch to a Ridge Regression baseline' if collinearity involves core descriptors. This violates FR-003 (System MUST train a Random Forest regressor) and Constitution Principle VII (Cross-Validation Rigor), which mandates the Random Forest protocol. Switching the model architecture to bypass data quality issues is a silent weakening of the core methodology.

Task T031 implements a 'Target Perturbation' sensitivity analysis (adding Gaussian noise to y) instead of the 'Threshold Sweep' required by FR-005 and SC-003. FR-005 explicitly requires 'sweeping a physically-grounded critical cooling rate cutoff'. The task's deliverable (RMSE variance across noise perturbations) does not satisfy the acceptance criteria for threshold stability.

Task T054 instructs the system to raise a ValueError if collinearity resolution fails after 3 drops. This contradicts the 'best_available' fallback logic in T029b which allows proceeding with an unstable model. This creates a logical contradiction where the pipeline is instructed to both proceed with a 'best available' model (T029b) and fail if that model is unstable (T054), violating the consistency of the acceptance criteria.

Tasks T057-T059 are marked 'FAILED: unspecified' and rely on audit scripts (T046-T049) that are not defined as executable deliverables in the task list. The plan assumes these artifacts exist to satisfy Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth), but the tasks do not define the execution logic to generate them, creating a deadlock where success criteria cannot be verified.
